summary: Use 32-byte signature references for principal signature relationships while retaining exact canonical candidate text

replay.detail: No claim replay is required. Existing signature relationships are converted from local stored data; canonical candidate text and lexical candidate ordering are preserved. Global nonce evidence and conflict semantics are unchanged.

schema.detail: Candidates retain their full original signature text and PRIMARY KEY(claim_id, signature). A new claim_signature_originals dictionary stores another exact text copy, candidate provenance and a 32-byte SHA-256 reference, keyed by (claim_id, reference). Sources, the selected-signature facade and judging cursors move to references; the migration checkpoint records staged progress. The dictionary duplicates canonical text and adds key/row overhead: smaller relationship values do not establish total database savings. No measured size or latency result is claimed.

rules.detail: Signature verification, canonical candidate selection and global nonce admission rules do not change. A reference does not replace the original signed text as evidence.

compatibility.detail: The local principal storage representation and storage version change; signed claim bytes and peer wire formats do not. Existing inline TEXT and new BLOB references share one compatibility reader during conversion. Local data is preserved rather than discarded or reconstructed from remote peers. Older binaries that do not support this storage version must not open the upgraded store.

downtime.detail: After authorization bootstrap completes, the upgrade performs online reference migration in batches of at most 64 rows per advance, with persistent cursors for candidates, sources, facade and judging stages, rather than a whole-store conversion transaction or history-sized index build. Reference migration progress is reported separately from authorization readiness. Migration and dictionary writes add local work; row bounds are not encoded-byte or elapsed-time bounds. No migration duration, startup bound or latency improvement is claimed.

manual.detail: No manual claim replay or database deletion is required.

recovery.detail: Each migration page and its progress commit atomically; interruption resumes from the persisted cursor while preserving canonical candidates and global nonce evidence. New writes emit references during conversion. Keep a pre-upgrade backup for rollback rather than opening the changed schema with an unsupported older binary.
